story_title: Category, Vendor, and Part Search Filters
requirement_text: S6-R8: Part search.** The toolbar has a part search input built on the **reports suite's shared toolbar search pattern** — a page-local search field in the report's own toolbar, not the application's global search bar (the same page-local toolbar-search affordance used elsewhere in the reports suite; Parts Velocity is the sibling that searches part number and description). It narrows the report to parts whose **part number or description** contains the entered text, case-insensitively, and applies server-side (S6-R5).

story_title: Category, Vendor, and Part Search Filters
requirement_text: S6-R9:** The Date range (Story 5), Location (Story 7), Category, Vendor, and part search combine with AND — a part must satisfy every active filter and the search to appear. _* Context note: every filter on this report is server-side. The Date range (Story 5), Location (Story 7), Category filter, Vendor filter, and part search each reload the report from the server; only the column selection (Story 8) is a purely client-side view choice._ * * *

S7-R1:** The toolbar has a location filter labeled "Location" — a multi-select, and the rightmost filter — listing the locations the signed-in user has access to, with an "All locations" / "Clear all" toggle.
S7-R2:** On a first visit (no saved selection — Story 8), it defaults to the user's currently active location.
S7-R3:** Selecting one, several, or all locations **reloads** the report scoped to that set.
S7-R4:** Scoping is always constrained to the user's accessible locations; a location the user cannot access is never included.
S7-R5:** If the requested location set resolves to none the user can access, the report falls back to the user's currently active location.

S7-R6:** The report includes a per-row **Location** column that is shown only when the current scope spans more than one location; when a single location is in scope the column is hidden. Its visibility follows the location scope automatically and it is not one of the columns offered in the column-selection control (Story 8).

S7-R7:** When the Location column is shown, each row's Location cell names the location that row's part stock is held at. Because each row is one part at one location (S2-R2, S2-R3), every row maps to exactly one location — the report never shows an aggregated "Multiple" value in this column. **Negative Cases:**
S7-N1:** A user with access to only one location still sees the filter with a single selectable location.
S7-N2:** If the selected location(s) hold no in-stock parts on the resolved date, the report shows the no-data message (Story 12). * * *
S8-R1:** A column-selection control — an icon button whose tooltip reads "Column Selection" — lets the user toggle each column on or off.
S8-R2:** The **Total Cost** column is always shown and cannot be turned off.
S8-R3:** Every other column is available in the control; Margin and Total Sell are off by default, the rest on by default (S3-R12).
S8-R4:** Whatever columns are shown, they appear in the fixed left-to-right order of S3-R1 (toggling visibility never reorders columns), with Total Cost always last.

S8-R5:** The report remembers, in the user's browser, the selected date range, category selection, vendor selection, part search text, location selection, column selection, and sort, and restores them on the user's next visit.

S8-R6:** Restore is defensive: a saved value that is no longer valid falls back to that setting's default rather than breaking the view. A saved category or vendor no longer present in the data is dropped. _* Context note: persistence is per-browser (not tied to the user's account); it persists across visits in the same browser but does not follow the user to another browser or device._ * * *
S9-R1:** On first load (and after any data reload), the rows are sorted by Total Cost, highest first (descending). The server applies this default order.

S9-R2:** Every column is sortable by clicking its header. Clicking a column that is not the active sort sorts it ascending; clicking the active sort column again toggles it to descending. There is no third "cleared" state. Sorting is resolved **server-side** : each header click re-fetches the data ordered by the chosen column and direction, returning the **first page** of the re-sorted result set.
S9-R3:** Money and numeric columns sort by their underlying value; text columns (Part #, Description, Category, Vendor) sort as text, case-insensitively.
S9-R4:** Sorting reorders the data rows only; the totals row stays at the bottom.

S9-R5:** The user's chosen sort is remembered per browser and restored on return (Story 8). _* Context note: unlike the reports whose sort resets each visit, this report remembers the user's sort along with the rest of its setup (Story 8)._ * * *
S10-R1:** The toolbar has a menu, opened from a three-dot button, holding the download options.
S10-R2:** The menu has an option labeled "Download (PDF)" and an option labeled "Download (CSV)".
S10-R3:** Both downloads include only the columns currently shown, in the same left-to-right order as the screen, with Total Cost last.
S10-R4:** Both downloads honor the current date, category, vendor, location, and part-search filters.
S10-R5:** Both downloads apply the current sort.
S10-R6:** Both downloads include a totals row matching the on-screen totals (the full-filtered-set totals, S4-R2), labeled "Totals".
S10-R7:** Money and Margin % use two-decimal and one-decimal formats respectively; an undefined Margin % shows "—".

S10-R8:** The PDF header shows the report name "Inventory Value", the organization name, the selected period, and an "as of" line naming the day the values represent (or a message that no snapshot is available for the period).
S10-R9:** The PDF shows the shop logo at the top when one is set; the CSV never includes a logo.
S10-R10:** The downloaded files are named "inventory-value-report.pdf" and "inventory-value-report.csv".

S10-R11: Server-side generation.** Both exports are generated **server-side** against the current filters, part search, and sort — the full filtered set, not only the loaded page. The export is not built from the rows currently in the browser.

S10-R12: Export size guardrail.** To keep a single-shot export renderable, an export is capped at a maximum of **10,000 rows** in the filtered set. When the current filtered set exceeds the cap, neither the PDF nor the CSV is produced; instead the user sees the message: **" This report is too large to export. Narrow the date range or filters, then try again."** [Cap value 10,000 is a proposed default — confirm the exact suite-standard value with the owner before dev.]

S10-R15:** Every export (each CSV and each PDF) includes the **Location** column whenever it is shown on screen (S7-R6), and always includes a "Locations:" line naming the location or locations the report is scoped to, or "All locations" when every location the user has access to is selected — matching the on-screen scope. In a PDF the "Locations:" line appears in the header area; in a CSV it appears as a leading metadata line above the column-header row. **Error Handling:**

requirement_text: S10-R13:** On a successful download the user sees a success notification: "Inventory Value report exported (PDF)" or "Inventory Value report exported (CSV)".

S10-R14:** If a download fails, the user sees an error notification: "Failed to export inventory value report (pdf)" or "Failed to export inventory value report (csv)". _* Context note: in the CSV, money values are written as plain numbers with two decimals and no thousands separators (so they parse cleanly in a spreadsheet); the PDF uses the same on-screen currency formatting with the "$" and thousands separators._ * * *

S11-R1:** Once per day, overnight, the system records — for every location across every organization — one row per then-in-stock, non-core part, capturing its identity (part, category, vendor), on-hand quantity, unit cost, unit sell, total cost, and total sell, stored to the cent, under that day's calendar date.

S11-R2:** The parts captured use the same in-stock, non-core scope as the live report (Story 2), and the same valuation (Story 3), so a recorded day equals what the live report would have shown that day.

S11-R3:** Re-running the capture for a date replaces that date's rows for each location (the existing rows for that location and date are removed, then re-inserted from current data). The capture is idempotent and self-healing from current data.
S11-R4:** A location with no in-stock parts on a date simply has no rows for that date (this is valid, not an error).

S11-R5:** History accrues forward only from the first capture; there is no backfill of dates before capture began, and a re-run always records current truth under the current date — it cannot reconstruct a past date.

S11-R6: Snapshot retention.** Captured snapshots are retained at reducing granularity as they age, measured from the current date: * **0 –13 months old:** every daily capture is kept — full daily per-part detail. This covers the report's longest date preset (366 days / This Year / Last Year) entirely at daily resolution. * **older than 13 months:** reduced to **monthly** — only the last capture of each calendar month is retained; the other daily captures in this band are pruned.
